public_repository_exposure.finding: Every owner repository visible to this session is PUBLIC on GitHub (sift-alpha and the NBA, NHL, CBB, NFL, CFB sport repositories). The sport repositories track raw provider data on their main and data branches: for example nba-edge-finder data/history/espn (ESPN box scores, play-by-play, shot events), NHL-edge-finder data/history including data/history/moneypuck/shots_*.parquet, the Kalshi board and quote archives, and the official NBA injury-report rows. The rights registry treats these archives as 'internal research only'. A public repository is not internal: publishing raw provider data is redistribution, which is the one use that nearly every provider's terms restrict (MoneyPuck's listed downloads are recorded as non-commercial research only; Kalshi's developer agreement bars sharing API data with third parties without written permission).
public_repository_exposure.owner_decision_needed: Decide whether the sport repositories (or at least their raw-data paths and data branches) should be private, or whether the raw archives should move to private storage. This session cannot and did not change repository visibility or access. Not legal advice.
public_repository_exposure.what_is_not_affected: Alpha's own published dashboard and research artifacts commit aggregates, counts and digests only (enforced by tests); builder and challenger work on the archive is internal use.

It requires Kalshi membership and gives no research carve-out. A separate Kalshi data terms of service exists but was not retrieved, so public-endpoint rules may differ.

terms.lead_note: Lead note: the agent's PROHIBITED reading is the strict one. Clause 3.1 as quoted allows collecting and storing API data 'for purposes of facilitating your own trading on Kalshi'; research that informs the owner's own trading plausibly falls inside that, research for any other purpose does not, and sharing API data with third parties needs Kalshi's written permission. Two owner questions follow: (1) is every use of archived Kalshi data in these repositories in support of the owner's own trading, and (2) do any PUBLIC repository files or the public dashboard expose raw Kalshi API data (series listings, rules text, quotes) rather than aggregates. Not legal advice; no tier changed.
